0x90e6: pass the byte on only when the gate is set
takes a byte argument and calls 0x90BE with it, but only when the word at 0x3E1948 is non-zero; otherwise it returns having done nothing. A gate on one global. Read at 0x90E6-0x90FE.
0x19cd0: set a record's bytes at zero and two

takes a record pointer and two byte arguments and stores them at offsets 0 and 2. The `rol.l #4,d0` between them is dead - d0 is overwritten by the very next instruction - so it computes nothing; do not read meaning into it. Read at 0x19CD0-0x19CE4.
0xf52c: fill a sixteen-byte slot with a word

indexes 0x3E3F40 by d1 times sixteen and writes d0 into eight consecutive words there, which is exactly that slot. The loop is dbmi, not dbra, and move.w sets N from the value being stored - so a negative d0 stops it after the first word. Register arguments, no stack frame. Read at 0xF52C-0xF540.
0x193f2: set a record's first two bytes and clear its seventh

takes a record pointer and two byte arguments, writes them at offsets 0 and 1 through a post-incrementing pointer, then clears the byte at offset 6 - the displacement is 4 from the already-advanced pointer, which is easy to misread as offset 4. Read at 0x193F2-0x19404.
0x1485c: takes a cue index and a second long, rejects any index above 22 by returning 0xFF, and otherwise reads a word from the table at 0x1D616 to drive the sequencer. It holds 0x3E34CC in a2, 0x3E3536 in a4 and 0x143B0 in a3 - and 0x3E34CC is the pointer the goal statement names as being stored at 0x3E3268 and 0x3E3288 around frame 276, so this is the routine at the centre of that. Reached through the trampoline at 0x18A. 474 bytes; read the head at 0x1485C-0x1489E.
0xe546: pushes 0 and 0x13 and calls the sound-cue starter through the trampoline at 0x18A. Nothing else - a named shorthand for one cue. Read at 0xE546-0xE554.
0xe554: the same as 0xE546 with 0x12 instead of 0x13. Read at 0xE554-0xE562.
0x1867c: jump through the slot only if it holds a trampoline

takes a pointer and compares the word there against 0x4EF9, the encoding of `jmp <abs>.l`. If it matches it jumps to that address; otherwise it returns zero without calling anything. 0x4EF9 is exactly the signature describe.py uses to find the trampoline block below the first routine, so this is a guarded dispatch: the slot is only entered when it really does hold a jump stub. Read at 0x1867C-0x1868C.
0xfb74: return the argument as a pointer

one move and an rts, returning the first stack argument in a0. The map's twelve-byte extent covers a second identical fragment at 0x0FB7A, so the run is two copies of the same two instructions. Read at 0x0FB74-0x0FB80.
0x122b2: decoder state: emit d0, then d3

writes d0 to the destination and points a2 at 0x122BC. The whole-byte counterpart of the nibble pair at 0x1228C/0x1229E - same two-state machine held in a2, but emitting two registers in turn rather than splitting one byte. Read at 0x122B2-0x122BC.
0x122bc: decoder state: emit d3, then d0
the other half of 0x122B2: writes d3 and points a2 back. Read at 0x122BC-0x122C6.
0x17ed4: a shared epilogue: movem.l from -0x24(a6) into d2-d6 and a2-a4, unlk a6, rts. The larger sibling of 0x7866, which restores only d2 and a2. Routines jump here to return. Read at 0x17ED4-0x17EDE.
0x19c00: fill bytes with a long count

memset. Fills count+1 bytes at the pointer with the given byte and returns the original pointer, using the same dbra plus `subi.l #$10000` extension as the copy at 0x19BC2 so the count can exceed 65,535. Read at 0x19C00-0x19C22.
0x19c22: set the status register and return the old one

reads the status register into d0, writes the word it was given into it, and returns the previous value - the save-and-restore primitive for the interrupt mask, and the routine that raises or lowers it. Worth noting against 0x15A0, which carried the name 'interrupt mask set' until 2026-07-31 and does nothing of the kind: it ORs and ANDs a word in work RAM. This is the one that touches the mask. Read at 0x19C22-0x19C2E.
0x1868c: strlen. Scans forward from the pointer it is given until it reads a zero byte, then returns the distance minus one. The minus one is `moveq #$ff,d0`, which sign-extends to -1 rather than loading 255 - read it as 255 and the routine looks like it returns the length plus 256. Read at 0x1868C-0x1869E.
0x19bc2: copy bytes with a long count

a byte copy whose count is a full long, not a word: dbra handles the low sixteen bits and `subi.l #$10000` with a bcc repeats that for each higher unit, which is the standard way to run a dbra loop past 65,535. Read at 0x19BC2-0x19BD8.
0x197d8: divide a long by a word

the 68000's divu only takes a 32-bit dividend and gives a 16-bit quotient, so this does it in two halves - divide the high word, keep the remainder in place, divide the low - and negates the result when a0 is negative. Read at 0x197D8-0x197F4.
0x1940a: clear an eight-kilobyte band of the playfield

takes a byte, shifts it left twelve (swap then lsr.l #4, which is how the 68000 gets a sixteen-bit shift cheaply), adds that to 0x200004 and clears 0x800 longs from there - eight kilobytes, sixteen playfield rows at the 0x200 stride. Read at 0x1940A-0x1942A.
0x4dd2: give every player in play its own colour byte

walks the three structs at 0x3E1968 alongside a byte table at 0xFE0A stepped one per player, and for each whose field 0 has bits 14/15 set calls 0xC832 - a palette writer - with that player's byte and the constants 1, 3, 4. Companion to 0x4A6A, which walks the same players but calls the other palette writer 0xC688 with the table at 0xFE18 and indices 5, 6, 7. Read at 0x4DD2-0x4E20.
0x7d80: post each active player's entry and set state two

walks the three structs at 0x3E1968 alongside the pointer table at 0x215A6, and for each whose field 0 has bit 15 set calls 0x41BE with that pointer, the player index and the constants 12, 7 and 1, then stamps byte 0x1A with 2 - the same state 0xCD0C sets when a record's countdown expires. Note the gate is bit 15 alone, not bits 14/15 as its neighbours use. Read at 0x7D80-0x7DCE.
0x1a14e: drain one byte from the ring and service three channels

the reader for the ring 0x1A0CC writes: read pointer at 0x3E3D56, write pointer at 0x3E3D5A, and the buffer 0x3E3D46-0x3E3D55 with the same wrap. When the two pointers meet the ring is empty and it skips the read; otherwise it advances, takes the byte and hands it to 0x1A1CA. Either way it then calls 0x1A100 for channels 0, 1 and 2, and bumps a counter at 0x3E36D4. Read at 0x1A14E-0x1A19A.
0x1545c: centre two strings in the forty-two column field

measures both strings with 0x1868C - strlen - subtracts each length from 0x2A, halves the remainder and passes it to 0x17FCC before drawing. 0x2A is 42, the board's width in cells, so text is centred across the same grid the playfield uses. Read at 0x1545C-0x154A8.
0x8a24: is the run of cells free

builds a step as (dy shifted left five) plus dx - the board's row stride is 0x20 - resolves the starting cell through 0x11BD8, and walks the given number of cells along that step. Each cell fails unless its low six bits are zero or exactly 0x30; anything else returns 0, and surviving the whole run returns 1. So a cell's low six bits are its occupancy and 0x30 is a value a piece may sit on. This is the can-it-be-placed test. Read at 0x8A24-0x8A70.
0x9034: commit the current player's pending piece

does nothing unless the current player's field 0x24 - the long 0x592A seeds from the rotation table - is non-zero. Then it calls 0x8BB2 with the struct and 1, calls 0x686, registers the struct twice through 0xEEEE with 0x11AD0 and 0xEE90 with 0x11ACA, and finishes with 0x90E6 and 0x19. Read at 0x9034-0x9080.
0x1b11c: strobe the control register through its shadow

offsets the caller's pointer by 0x1E0000 to reach a hardware register, sets 0x3E3D6C to 7, clears the four words 0x3E3D72 through 0x3E3D78, then writes the shadow word at 0x3E3D8E twice: once with bit 4 masked off, then with bits 4 and 0x400 set. A RAM shadow is how you read-modify-write a register that cannot be read, and writing it twice with one bit differing is a strobe rather than two settings. Read at 0x1B11C-0x1B166.
0x848e: clear each active player's pair at 0x30

walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, and for each whose field 0 has bits 14/15 set clears bytes 0x30 and 0x31, registers the struct through 0xEE90 with 0x11B36, and calls 0x8326 with it. Read at 0x848E-0x84DA.
0x1978e: the signed front end to the division 0x197D8 does: it takes the absolute value of each operand, carries the eventual sign in a0 by exclusive-or, and when the divisor is 0x10000 or more runs a sixteen-step shift-and-subtract long division by hand (add.l then addx.l to shift a 64-bit numerator, compare, conditionally subtract). Below that it falls through to 0x197D8's divu pair. Negates the quotient at the end when the signs differed. Read at 0x1978E-0x197D8.
0xb2e8: release the slot and drop the count

does nothing when the record's field 0x4 is already null. Otherwise it calls 0xB5B8 with the record's word at 0xC and two fives, stamps 0xFF into byte 1 of whatever field 0x4 points at, decrements byte 0x16 of the record at 0x3E1C84, then clears field 0x4, sets byte 0xD to 0xFF and clears byte 0. Field 0x4 going to zero is exactly the free marker 0xB2B0 and 0xB2CC search for, so this is the release matching those allocators, and 0x3E1C84's byte 0x16 is the live count. Read at 0xB2E8-0xB330.
0x3e3e: claim a slot at 0x3E0DF6 and fill it

walks the eight-byte slots at 0x3E0DF6 until it finds one whose first long is zero - the free marker - and fills it: the caller's long at offset 0, a byte pair at 4 and 5, a word at 6. Then it calls 0x3E84 with the slot and registers it through 0xEE90 with 0x11B3C. This is the allocator for the sixteen-slot table 0x3E26 wipes; note the search is unbounded, so a full table walks off the end. Read at 0x3E3E-0x3E84.
0x3da0: score three neighbours with weights one, one and two

the sibling of 0x3DE8 over the same board stride of 0x20. It adds 1 when the byte one before the cell matches either of two values, 1 more when the byte 0x1F on does, and 2 when the byte 0x21 back does, returning the total. Between them the two routines weight four neighbours 1, 1, 2, 4 and 8 - a directional encoding, not a count. Read at 0x3DA0-0x3DE8.
0x1e6dc: decompress the tile with this id

the indexed form of 0x11EFE: it looks the caller's tile id up in the word table at 0x2161A to get an offset, adds that to the tile set at 0xD2608, seeds d4 with 7 for the eight-pixel column, calls the decompressor, and returns the destination advanced by 8. So 0x2161A maps a tile id to its position in the compressed set, and 0x11EFE is the same thing when the caller already has the offset. Read at 0x1E6DC-0x1E720.
0x1942a: replace the high nibble of eight rows

builds a long from the caller's byte repeated four times, then walks 0x400 longs from 0x200004 plus the second byte shifted left twelve - 4096 bytes, eight rows at the 0x200 stride - keeping each long's low nibbles (mask 0x0F0F0F0F) and replacing the high ones. A recolour that preserves whatever the low nibble encodes. Read at 0x1942A-0x1946E.
0x404a: draw at the pixel coordinate, origin offset by four

turns a pair of words into a playfield address as 0x200004 plus (y - 4) shifted left nine - the 0x200 row stride - plus (x - 4), then blits through 0x11EF2 with a size of 0x80 and a source read from 0x34604. The -4 on both axes is the same offset that makes the playfield base 0x200004 rather than 0x200000: there is a four-pixel border the coordinates exclude. Read at 0x404A-0x408E.
0xbb38: find the record whose key at offset twelve matches

walks the sixteen fourteen-byte records at 0x3E1AE6 - the table 0xB2B0 allocates from, where a zero long at offset 4 means free - comparing the caller's word against each record's word at offset 0xC, and returns the record or null. So offset 0xC is that table's lookup key. Read at 0xBB38-0xBB7C.
0x910e: alternate between two values on a four-step counter

does nothing unless the word at 0x3E1948 is set - the same gate 0x90E6 checks. Then it picks the first byte argument when bit 0 of the counter at 0x3E1946 is set and the second when it is clear, passes the choice to 0x90BE, and advances that counter modulo 4. Two phases driven by a four-step cycle, so the other bit selects something this routine does not use. Read at 0x910E-0x9150.
0x4d90: post the record five past the index

scales its argument plus five by 32 - asl.l #4 then a doubling, the cheap way to multiply by 32 - indexes the table at 0x1F040 with it, steps two bytes in, and hands that pointer to 0xC724 along with the argument plus nine and the constants 1, 4, 1 and 8, then calls 0x4D6C. So 0x1F040 is a table of 32-byte records and this addresses one at a fixed offset from the caller's index. Read at 0x4D90-0x4DD2.
0x18000: the tail that stores the signed pair

the closing half of a computation that ends by writing 0x3E3D7B and 0x3E3D7A - the two bytes 0x154DE forwards, sign-extended, to 0x15504. It halves a difference into d2, stores d4 as the first byte, calls 0x18B76 with four longs, then adds d2 minus one to the result and stores that as the second. Both are signed, which is why the forwarder extends them. Read at 0x18000-0x18040.
0x11ea: the row step of the cell walk

the closing half of a nested loop: it advances three address registers and two frame locals by 0x20 - the board's row stride - a fourth by 8 and a fifth by 2, then bumps the inner counter against d6 and, when that runs out, the outer against the word at 0x16(a6). Two counters, five cursors, one row apart each pass. Read at 0x11EA-0x122C.
0xea7a: which of the seven candidates is this record's pair

follows the record's field 0x4A - the candidate list 0x18FA draws starting positions from - and compares each of up to seven two-byte entries against the record's own pair at 0x48/0x49, returning the index it matched at (or 7 if none did). 0xEA68 calls this and stores the answer at 0x3E1956, so the carry-over flag is that index rather than a boolean. Read at 0xEA7A-0xEABA.
0xefba: is this pair already in the event queue

the two-key form of 0xF000: same queue - count at 0x3E1CF4, twelve-byte entries from 0x3E1CF6 - but an entry only matches when both the long at offset 4 and the long at offset 8 equal the caller's two. So queue entries are keyed on a pair, and 0xF000 is the single-key lookup over the same structure. Read at 0xEFBA-0xEFFA.
0x130b0: run one memory test with interrupts masked

raises the interrupt mask to level 7 (sr = 0x2700), reads a descriptor - count, then two pointers, then a selector word - and jumps to ramTestAllPatterns at 0x1378E or to 0x1397A depending on that word, returning through a `lea $X(pc),a4` continuation rather than a call. It drops the mask back to 0x2000 before returning. This is the self-test driver, and the masking is why the service-switch pattern behaves unlike the others: for its duration no frame interrupt arrives at all. Read at 0x130B0-0x130EE.
0x8536: dissolve the screen and draw the banner

calls 0x11E10 - the screen dissolve describe.py names - then the 0xFDC2 sequence at 0x5020, then 0x4E82 with -1, then blits the image at 0xB5B30 to 0x200004 plus 0x3020, which at the 0x200 stride is row 24, column 32. Finishes with 0x90E6 and 0x15. Read at 0x8536-0x8576.
0xcd0c: the countdown's expiry: mark the record and pause

the action 0xCCB2 fires when byte 0x21 of a record reaches zero. It reads the record's player number from byte 0x2, calls 0x41BE with the caller's long, that number and the constants 12, 8 and 1, then stamps byte 0x1A of the record with 2 and writes 0x46 - seventy - into 0x3E1950, the pause flag describe.py already names, before calling 0x7A02. So the timer expiring pauses the game for seventy frames and moves the record to state 2. Read at 0xCD0C-0xCD4A.
0x778a: reads the record's player number from byte 0x2 and maps it through the owner-code table at 0x1000A. If byte 0x15 is zero it answers 1 outright; otherwise it asks 0x7870 for a cell using that owner code and answers 1 only when the byte there is not negative (sge then neg turns the condition into a clean 0 or 1). Read at 0x778A-0x77C8.
0x3de8: score the neighbours one stride either side

takes a cell pointer and two byte values to match. It adds 4 when the byte at offset 0x21 equals either, and 8 when the byte at offset -0x1F does - the same column one stride of 0x20 forward and back - and returns the total. A neighbour-adjacency score. It has the same shape as the deliberate wallCellSet change, which neutralises a `+ 0x4` on d3 - but checked and it is NOT this routine: wallCellSet is at 0x0255C, and this is a sibling with the same idiom. Two routines score neighbours this way; only the other one is edited. Read at 0x3DE8-0x3E26.
0x362a: draw an image column by column

hands 0x11EFE - the routine that decompresses one eight-pixel column from the tile set at 0xD2608 - to 0x357A together with a source, a destination and three sizes. So 0x357A is a generic driver that walks something and calls a per-column callback, and this is the tile-decompressing instance of it. 0x8576 reaches the same driver with different constants. Read at 0x362A-0x3666.
0xc206: find the entry matching this word

walks the thirty-two two-byte entries at 0x3E1C44 comparing each against the caller's word, returning the entry's address or null when none matches. The lookup half of the same table 0xC1EE allocates from - that one finds a slot whose first byte is negative, this one finds a slot by value. Read at 0xC206-0xC240.
0x66d4: the tail of the full-screen cell scan

the closing half of a nested loop: the inner counter runs to 0x1E stepping a playfield cursor by 0x1000 each time, the outer to 0x2A stepping 8 and unwinding 0x1E000. With the 8 by 8 cell grid 0x18CDE establishes - 0x1000 is eight screen rows at the 0x200 stride, 8 is eight pixels - that is 30 by 42 cells, or 240 by 336 pixels: the whole visible screen. So the board is scanned as 42 columns of 30 cells. Read at 0x66D4-0x670E.
0x1829c: write a colour into the first palette bank

takes an index and a colour word and stores the colour as two bytes at 0x3C0000 + index*4 and + index*4 + 2 - high byte first, then low. That is the layout system.ts describes from the other side: palette RAM is byte-wide on a sixteen-bit bus, so one colour occupies the high bytes of two consecutive words four bytes apart, and reading it as a single word at stride two takes the right red with the wrong green and blue. This is the ROM writing exactly that. Read at 0x1829C-0x182D4.
0x182d4: write a colour into the palette's upper half

identical to 0x1829C but based at 0x3C0400. That is not a second bank - entries are four bytes, so 0x400 is entry 256, and system.ts reads 1024 entries spanning 0x3C0000-0x3C1000. It is the same palette, indexed from 256 up. Finding it exposed a gap in compose.test.ts, which was snapshotting only 0x3C0000-0x3C0800 and therefore comparing half the palette. Read at 0x182D4-0x1830C.
0x15914: find the nth colon-separated field of a string

indexes the pointer table at 0x1DAF8 by the first word times four, returns null when that slot is null, and otherwise walks forward past the second word's worth of fields - a field ending at a colon (0x3A) or at the terminating zero. Running off the end returns null too. So 0x1DAF8 is a table of colon-delimited strings and this addresses one field of one entry. Read at 0x15914-0x1594C.
0x8878: hand the current player over and step on

reads the current player through the pointer at 0x3E1960, sets bit 14 of its field 0, passes its word at 0x48 to 0x6988, then calls 0x8A70 - the take-out-of-play routine - with the struct and that same word, followed by 0x5168 and 0x90E6 with 0x51. The bit-14 set before a take-out is worth noting rather than smoothing: this raises the in-play bit and then immediately runs the retirement path. Read at 0x8878-0x88B0.
0x19366: record whether the vector holds a stub, then clear a band

sets 0x3E340E to 1 only when the byte at 0x372 is non-zero *and* the word at 0x300 is 0x4EF9 - the encoding of `jmp <abs>.l`, the same trampoline signature 0x1867C tests before dispatching through a slot. So this is a presence check on an optional vector, remembered as a flag. It then clears forty-two rows of fifteen longs from the playfield base, stepping four bytes between rows. Read at 0x19366-0x1939C.
0x2300: clear the playfield and the first palette entry

zeroes the long at 0x3C0000, forces its start address even (btst #0 then subq, since a word store needs alignment), and clears from 0x200004 to 0x21E004 eight words at a time - the loop body is unrolled to sixteen bytes rather than counted. That range is 0x1E000, most of the 0x20000 playfield. Read at 0x2300-0x2338.
0xca52: walk the whole list with the flag raised

holds the mode byte at 0x3E2498 at 1 for the duration and walks the circular list headed at 0x3E20A0 - a second head beside the 0x3E20A8 one 0xC504 takes from - calling 0xC538 on every node until it returns to the head. It reads each node's next pointer into a2 *before* the call, which is the safe-iteration shape: the callee is allowed to unlink the node it is handed. Read at 0xCA52-0xCA88.
0x18cde: address the eight by eight cell on the playfield

builds a playfield address as 0x200004 plus row times 4096 plus column times 8, then calls 0x1E6DC with it, the caller's pointer, and a word raised by 0x13. Row times 4096 is eight screen rows at the 0x200 stride and column times 8 is eight pixels, so the game addresses the playfield as a grid of 8 by 8 cells. The row scale is done as swap-then-lsr.l #4, the cheap sixteen-bit shift. Read at 0x18CDE-0x18D14.
0x472a: run the four-step sequence on the record at 0x1F420

calls 0x450C four times with the same record, 0x1F420, and the indices 0, 1, 4 and 7. Nothing else - a fixed script. The gaps in the index list are the interesting part: whatever 0x450C selects, this record uses four of the slots and skips the rest. Read at 0x472A-0x4760.
0x5020: run the sequence on 0xFDC2, with a different routine at index five

calls 0x450C with the record 0xFDC2 at indices 0, 1 and 2, but routes index 5 through 0x452E instead. So the two routines are alternatives over the same (record, index) shape and the choice is per step, not per record - which is what distinguishes this from 0x472A's uniform script. Read at 0x5020-0x5056.
0x14dc: run the handler for every flag bit set

takes the word at 0x3E0DC6, clears it, and walks its sixteen bits from the top: each iteration shifts left and, when the result is negative, calls the routine whose pointer sits at the matching slot of the table at 0xFCF6. So 0x3E0DC6 is a pending-work bitmask and 0xFCF6 is its sixteen handlers - which is what 0x1578 and 0x1592 are really doing when they set and clear bits there: posting and cancelling work. Clearing the word before dispatching means a handler that posts again is served on the next pass, not this one. Read at 0x14DC-0x1512.
0x1a0cc: push a byte into the second ring

the same shape as 0x1A19A over a different ring: pointer at 0x3E3D5A, buffer 0x3E3D46-0x3E3D55, read pointer at 0x3E3D56. It advances the pointer first, wraps, and returns 1 without storing when the pointer has caught the reader - so this one reports the drop where 0x1A19A silently discards. Read at 0x1A0CC-0x1A100.
0xc504: take the first item from the list, or zero when empty

reads the long at 0x3E20A8 and returns zero when it points at 0x3E20A8 itself - so the list is circular and empty is the head pointing at itself, not null. Otherwise it raises the mode flag at 0x3E2498 around a call to 0xC4E8 with that item and returns it. Together with 0xC4CA, which links a node in with next at offset 4 and previous at offset 0, this makes 0x3E20A8 a circular doubly-linked list head. Read at 0xC504-0xC538.
0xccb2: tick the record's countdown and fire when it expires

calls 0x90E6 with 100, then - if byte 0x21 of the record is not already zero - decrements it and, only on the step that reaches zero, calls 0xCD0C with the long at 0x21562 and the record. Byte 0x21 is the field 0x15BE arms with 5 when it resets a record, so this is that timer running down and the expiry action. Read at 0xCCB2-0xCCE6.
0x1a19a: push a byte into the ring, dropping it when full

the write pointer lives at 0x3E3D66. It stores the byte, advances the pointer, wraps back to 0x3E3D5E once the pointer passes 0x3E3D61, and then - if the new pointer has caught the read pointer at 0x3E3D62 - puts the old pointer back, which discards the byte just written rather than overrunning. So the ring is the four bytes 0x3E3D5E-0x3E3D61 and a full ring drops rather than blocks. Read at 0x1A19A-0x1A1CA.
0x1fd6: probe three slots and always answer two

calls 0x200A with 0, 1 and 2 in turn, stopping early if one returns 1. But d4 is set to 2 before the loop and never written again, so the value returned is 2 whatever the probe finds - the result is discarded and only 0x200A's side effects matter. Recorded rather than smoothed over: a reader who assumes the return reflects the search will be wrong. Read at 0x1FD6-0x200A.
0xe516: start both cues if each has enough

asks 0x184 about cue 0x13 and gives up unless it is at least 0x7D0, then about cue 0x12 unless it is at least 0xC8; only when both hold does it call 0xE546 and 0xE554 to start them, returning 1, and 0 otherwise. The same two ceilings 0xE562 and 0xE588 clamp to, which settles what that per-cue value is: a resource that is checked before it is spent. Read at 0xE516-0xE546.
0xf000: is this already in the event queue

reads the word at 0x3E1CF4 as a count and gives up when it is negative, then walks entries from 0x3E1CF6 twelve bytes apart comparing the long at offset 4 of each against the long the caller points at - returning 1 on a match and 0 when the count runs out. So the event queue at 0x3E1CF4 is a count followed by twelve-byte entries whose offset 4 is the key. Read at 0xF000-0xF030.
0xaec2: how many steps this kind takes

maps a word to a count: 0x11 gives 2, 0x24 gives 3, anything else gives 5 - then adds one when byte 0x1D of the record pointed at by 0x3E1964 has reached 3 or more. Two special kinds, a default, and a late-game increment. Read at 0xAEC2-0xAEF2.
0xc538: run it with the flag raised, then against the other buffer

saves the byte at 0x3E2498, sets it to 1, calls 0xC4E8 with its argument, puts the old value back, then calls 0xC4AE with 0x3E20A8 and the same argument. So 0x3E2498 is a mode flag the first call reads, and the work is done twice against two different buffers. Read at 0xC538-0xC568.
0x7d50: hand the table entry twelve past the index to 0x41BE

takes a word index, reads the long at 0x21516 indexed by (index + 12) times four, and calls 0x41BE with that pointer, the index, and the constants 12, 9 and 1. The +12 before scaling means the table's first twelve entries belong to something else. Read at 0x7D50-0x7D80.
0xac1c: raise the entry's counter by the phase step, or clear it

indexes the byte array at 0x3E1C9E. A negative entry is cleared to zero; otherwise the phase byte at 0x3E195C plus two, capped at 3, is added to it. So each entry accumulates faster in later phases and a negative value is the reset marker rather than a count. Read at 0xAC1C-0xAC4C.
0x14eca: read the six by twenty table, or 0xFF

takes two words, rejects a first at or above 6 and a second at or above 0x14 by returning 0xFF, and otherwise reads the byte at 0x3E3454 indexed as row times 20 plus column. So 0x3E3454 is a 6 by 20 byte table - 120 bytes - and 0xFF is its out-of-range answer rather than a value. Read at 0x14ECA-0x14EF8.
0x12368: the fixed-width sibling of 0x12078: instead of reading a width from the source's first two bytes it hardcodes 8, so the per-row advance is 0x200 minus 8, which is 0x1F8 - the same figure the tile decompressor uses to wrap a row. Returns the advanced source pointer. Read at 0x12368-0x1238C.
0x1235e: writes d7 to the destination and points a4 at 0x12354, completing the three-state cycle that 0x12354 and its partners run in the second instance of the decompressor's machine. Read at 0x1235E-0x12368.
0x11efe: decompress one eight-pixel column from the tile set

points a0 at 0xD2608 plus the offset it is given, takes the destination and a word, seeds d4 with 7 and d3 with 0, and calls graphicsDecompressor at 0x11F2A - then returns the destination advanced by 8. The 7 is the column counter graphicsDecompressor decrements with dbra, so a call covers eight pixels across, and 0xD2608 is where the compressed tiles live. Read at 0x11EFE-0x11F2A.
0xfc46: step the two-bit counter toward its target

exclusive-ors the bytes at 0x3E0DE6 and 0x3E0DE2 and, if they differ in bit 1, adds 2 to the second modulo 4 and stores it back - so 0x3E0DE2 walks two-bit values toward 0x3E0DE6. It also reads 0x146084 and 0x1461C0 without keeping either, both inside the protection window CLAUDE.md records as served by a state machine. Read at 0xFC46-0xFC74.
0x900a: sets bit 14 of the record's field 0 - one of the two bits every player walk tests before doing anything - then calls 0x592A to seed field 0x24 from the rotation table, calls 0x41BE with the long at 0x2157E, -1, 0 and 2, and returns 1. Read at 0x900A-0x9034.
0x8a70: take a record out of play

passes the record's field 0x7A pointer and a word to 0x88B0, calls 0x8BB2 with the record and a zero, stamps byte 0x22 with 0xFE, and clears bit 13 of field 0 (andi.w #$DFFF). Bit 14 is what 0x900A sets to bring a player in; this clears the bit below it, so field 0's high bits are a small state rather than a single flag. Read at 0x8A70-0x8A9C.
0x12078: blit an image whose first word is its width

takes a source and a destination. The first two bytes of the source are a big-endian width - assembled by hand, `move.b (a0)+` then `lsl.w #8` then `add.b (a0)+` - and the routine computes 0x200 minus it, which is the playfield row stride less the span, i.e. how far to step the destination at the end of each row. Then it runs the copy at 0x120A2 and returns the advanced source pointer. This is what 0x37D2 calls with 0xBB38A. Read at 0x12078-0x120A2.
0x744e: find the player's shot at this cell

takes a player struct and a coordinate pair, follows field 0x6A to that player's shot ring, and walks it comparing the first two bytes of each entry against the pair - returning the entry's address on a match and null when the ring ends. Entries are 0x1A bytes apart and the ring is terminated by an entry whose first byte is negative (bge continues while it is not). So a shot record is 26 bytes and its first two bytes are its cell. Read at 0x744E-0x747A.
0x19bd8: copy bytes safely when they overlap

memmove. Compares source against destination: when the source is lower it falls straight into the forward copy at 0x19BC2, otherwise it adds the count to both pointers and copies backward with pre-decrements, so an overlapping move does not eat its own tail. Same dbra plus `subi.l #$10000` extension for counts past 65,535. Read at 0x19BD8-0x19C00.
0x7e7a: award a thousand to the current player

stores its byte argument at 0x3E1AE2, then multiplies it by 126 - (x*2)<<6 minus x*2, which is the classic shift-and-subtract for a constant - and uses that to index 0x3E1968, adding 0x3E8 to the long at field 0xC. 126 is 0x7E, the player stride, so this identifies two things: **field 0xC of a player struct is a score**, and **0x3E1AE2 holds the current player's index**, sitting immediately past the three structs which end there. Read at 0x7E7A-0x7EA4.
0x154de: call through with the signed pair at 0x3E3D7A

forwards its argument to 0x15504 along with the bytes at 0x3E3D7B and 0x3E3D7A, each sign-extended to a long (ext.w then ext.l, so they are signed, not an index pair). Nothing else. Read at 0x154DE-0x15504.
0xe562: clamp cue nineteen to two thousand

asks 0x178 about cue 0x13 with a 1, and if the long that comes back is greater than 0x7D0 calls the cue starter through 0x18A with 0x13 and 0x7D0 - so it lowers the value to the ceiling and leaves anything at or under it alone. Pairs with 0xE546, which starts the same cue with zero. Read at 0xE562-0xE588.
0xe588: clamp cue eighteen to two hundred
the same shape as 0xE562 for cue 0x12 with a ceiling of 0xC8. The pair fixes what the cue starter's second argument is: a value with a per-cue maximum, not a flag. Read at 0xE588-0xE5AE.
0x660: wipe the board region and start the level

clears every byte from 0x3E0844 up to and including 0x3E0DC3 - which spans the board array at 0x3E0864-0x3E0DA4 and the words either side of it - then reads the level pointer at 0x3E0DCA, pushes the long it points at, and calls 0x6648 with it and a zero. Read at 0x660-0x686.
0xcce6: act on the record once, and only in the early phases

takes a record and does nothing unless the phase byte at 0x3E195C is 0 or 1 (bhi skips above 1) and bit 2 of the record's byte 0x19 is still clear. When both hold it sets that bit and calls 0xCDAE with the record - so byte 0x19 bit 2 is an already-done latch and the work happens at most once per record, never after the early phases. Read at 0xCCE6-0xCD0C.
0x3ccc: look up an entry in the table the top two bits select

a two-level lookup with register arguments. The top two bits of d3 (lsr.b #6) index the table of pointers at 0x20812; d5 scaled by four indexes into the pointer that comes back; the long there is the result. So 0x20812 holds four pointers and the pair (d3 high bits, d5) addresses one entry. Read at 0x3CCC-0x3CEE.
0x8576: blit a fixed image with its size to the playfield

calls 0x362A with five constants: source 0x333F6, destination 0x200004 four bytes into the playfield, and 0x2A, 0x1E, 0xF0. No parameters and no state. Distinct from 0x37D2, which blits 0xBB38A through 0x12078 with no size arguments at all. Read at 0x8576-0x8598.
0x592a: seed a record from the rotation table

takes a record pointer, copies the long at 0xFF90 into its field 0x24, then calls 0xEEEE with 0x11ACA and the record. 0xFF90 is the piece-rotation-group table describe.py already names, so field 0x24 starts out holding its first entry. What 0xEEEE does with the pair is unread. Read at 0x592A-0x5948.
0x12354: writes d4 to the destination and points a4 at 0x1235E. Part of the second instance of the decompressor's state machine, the one 0x1232E and 0x12340 belong to - state kept in a4 rather than a2. Read at 0x12354-0x1235E.
0x1e8be: process two units and step to the next four-kilobyte block

sets d3 to 1, calls 0x1E862, then advances a0 by 0xFE0. The arithmetic says what that means: 0x1000 - 0xFE0 is 0x20, so the callee consumed two sixteen-byte units and this steps the pointer on to the next 4 KB boundary. Read at 0x1E8BE-0x1E8C8.
0x1e8c8: process four units and step to the next four-kilobyte block
the same as 0x1E8BE with d3 set to 3 and a0 advanced by 0xFC0 - 0x1000 less four sixteen-byte units. The pair fixes both the unit size and the block size. Read at 0x1E8C8-0x1E8D2.
0x1865e: save the machine state for a later jump

setjmp. Takes a buffer pointer, reads the return address off the stack into d1, and movem.l's d1-d7 and a2-a7 into the buffer - so the buffer holds every callee-saved register plus where to come back to. Returns zero, which is the first-time return. Its partner is 0x1866C. Read at 0x1865E-0x1866C.
0x1866c: restore a saved state and jump back

longjmp. Takes the buffer 0x1865E filled and a value, movem.l's the registers back out of it, and writes the saved return address over the one on the stack so the rts lands in the original caller instead of this one. The value it was given is already in d0 and becomes that return's result. Read at 0x1866C-0x1867C.
0x17ede: wait until the long at 0x3E3532 changes

reads 0x3E3532, then compares it against itself in a loop, spinning while equal - so it blocks until something outside changes that long - and then calls 0x19C3C. A second wait distinct from the frame semaphore at 0x3E0802 that 0x512 uses. Read at 0x17EDE-0x17EF4.
0x160dc: takes a pointer and returns the bitwise or of the bytes at offsets 0, 1 and 2, zero-extended. Read at 0x160DC-0x160F8.
0x1228c: decoder state: emit the high nibble, then the low

fetches the next source byte, writes its high nibble plus d2 to the destination, and leaves a2 pointing at 0x1229E. The decompressor keeps its state in that register rather than in a variable: each state ends by naming its successor, and the caller jumps through a2. This is the `lea $X(pc),aN` continuation shape CLAUDE.md flags, and it is why each state needs its own decompiled function. Read at 0x1228C-0x1229E.
0x1229e: decoder state: emit the low nibble, then the high

the other half of 0x1228C. Writes the low nibble of the byte already fetched, plus d2, and points a2 back at 0x1228C so the next call fetches again. Two states alternating gives one byte per two output pixels. Read at 0x1229E-0x122AE.
0x1232e: second decoder state: emit the high nibble, then the low

the same alternation as 0x1228C over a different register set - source a3, byte d7, bias a5, continuation a4 - so the decompressor has two independent instances of the state machine. Read at 0x1232E-0x12340.
0x12340: second decoder state: emit the low nibble, then the high

the partner of 0x1232E, writing the low nibble of d7 plus a5 and pointing a4 back. Note the map's extent runs two instructions past the rts into 0x12350, which stores d4 and returns - a third fragment sharing the range. Read at 0x12340-0x12354.
0xf2ee: pointer from an offset into the record table
adds 0x1F7F0 to its argument, the exact inverse of 0xF2FA which subtracts it. Offset in, pointer out. Read at 0xF2EE-0xF2FA.
0x12066: shift eight pixels' colour by a delta

takes a pointer in a1 and a delta in d0, and for eight consecutive bytes replaces each with its low nibble plus the delta. Register arguments, no stack frame - an inner helper of 0x1204C. Read at 0x12066-0x12078.
0x1204c: shift an eight by two block's colour

calls 0x12066 on the pointer it is given and again 0x1F8 further on. 0x1F8 plus the eight bytes 0x12066 walks is 0x200, the playfield row stride, so this recolours two rows of eight pixels - an eight by two block. Read at 0x1204C-0x12066.
0xfc10: tst.w on 0x140000 and tst.l on 0x1432B0, both inside the window CLAUDE.md records as served by a state machine rather than plain memory. It keeps neither value; only the reads and the flags they leave. Compare 0xFC06, which reads 0x1400E8. Read at 0xFC10-0xFC1E.
0xe776: look up the value paired with a byte

walks the table at 0x11A90 a byte at a time until it finds one equal to the argument, then returns the byte after it. The table is therefore key/value pairs, and there is no bound on the search - a key that is not present runs off the end, so the table must be terminated by something the caller can only ever ask for. Read at 0xE776-0xE790.
0xe790: look up the byte paired with a value

the inverse of 0xE776 over the same table: starts one byte later at 0x11A91, scans for a match, and returns the byte before it. So 0xE776 maps key to value and this maps value back to key. Read at 0xE790-0xE7A8.
0xea68: work out and store the carry-over flag

passes its argument to 0xEA7A and stores the byte that comes back at 0x3E1956. That is the flag 0x1836 tests when deciding whether to skip one player during the new-game reset - the mechanism that carries a player over instead of wiping them. Read at 0xEA68-0xEA7A.
0xee22: translate one byte through the board table
reads the byte at 0x3E0DD2, uses it to index the table at 0x140034 in the board data region, and stores the result at 0x3E0DD4. A single translation between two globals. Read at 0xEE22-0xEE3A.
0xc4ca: link a node into the list after another

a doubly-linked list insert. Takes the node to insert and the node to insert after: saves the second's successor, points it at the new node, sets the new node's back link, gives it the saved successor, and fixes that successor's back link. So the links are next at offset 4 and previous at offset 0. Read at 0xC4CA-0xC4E8.
0xc1ee: find a free two-byte slot marked by a high bit

walks thirty-two two-byte slots from 0x3E1C44 and returns the first whose byte is negative, or null when none is (suba.l a0,a0). Note the convention differs from 0xB2B0 and 0xB2CC, where free means a zero long at offset 4: here it is the high bit of the first byte being set. Read at 0xC1EE-0xC206.
0xdabc: copy 1344 bytes and return the count
takes a source and a destination and moves 0x540 bytes one at a time with a dbra over 0x53F, counting as it goes and returning the count. Read at 0xDABC-0xDAD6.
0xb2cc: find a free slot in the moving-unit table

walks seven eighteen-byte slots from 0x3E1BC6 - the moving-unit table - and returns the address of the first whose long at offset 4 is zero, or null when every slot is taken (suba.l a0,a0 zeroes the register). So a long at +4 of zero means free. Read at 0xB2CC-0xB2E8.
0xb2b0: find a free fourteen-byte slot past the player structs

the same shape as 0xB2CC one table along: sixteen fourteen-byte slots from 0x3E1AE6, returning the first whose long at offset 4 is zero, or null when all are taken. 0x3E1AE6 sits just past the player structs, which end at 0x3E1AE2. Read at 0xB2B0-0xB2CC.
0x5dec: one move and an rts: returns the long at 0xC(a7), the third argument. Note the map gives this an eighteen-byte extent covering two more fragments of the same kind - 0x5DF2 returns the second argument and 0x5DF8 the first - so the run is three tiny accessors sharing one entry. Read at 0x5DEC-0x5DFE.
0x7866: restore d2 and a2 and unlink
a shared epilogue: movem.l from -0xC(a6) into d2 and a2, unlk a6, rts. No work of its own - routines jump here to return. Read at 0x7866-0x7870.
0x3e26: clear the sixteen-slot table and its flag

clears the first long of each of sixteen eight-byte slots from 0x3E0DF6 (dbra over 16, stepping a0 by 8), then clears the flag byte at 0x3E0E78 that 0x3F10 sets and 0x3F1A clears. Read at 0x3E26-0x3E3E.
0x3f10: one instruction: stores 1 in the byte at 0x3E0E78. The counterpart of 0x3F1A, which clears it; 0x3E26 also clears it after wiping the table at 0x3E0DF6. Read at 0x3F10-0x3F1A.
0x3f1a: one instruction: clears the byte at 0x3E0E78, the flag 0x3F10 raises. Read at 0x3F1A-0x3F22.
0x46c2: calls 0xC832 - a palette writer - with five constant arguments, 0, 1, 12, 7 and 2, and nothing else. No parameters and no state, so it writes the same entry every time. Read at 0x46C2-0x46E0.
0x4f8c: takes a source and a destination on the stack and moves sixteen words - thirty-two bytes - from one to the other with a dbra loop. No interpretation of the contents. Read at 0x4F8C-0x4F9E.
0x545a: read field six of the current record, or zero
tests the pointer at 0x3E0EC2 and, if it is not null, returns the word at offset 6 of the record it points to; returns zero when the pointer is null. A guarded accessor. Read at 0x545A-0x5474.
0x15be: reset a record and arm it with five

takes a record pointer on the stack, clears the long at 0x4 and the bytes at 0x19 and 0x1D, then stores 5 in byte 0x21. Byte 0x1D is the same field 0x1F60 counts down, so this is the record's initial state. Read at 0x15BE-0x15D6.
0x1f60: takes a record pointer and decrements its byte at 0x1D unless that byte is already zero (bls, so unsigned). The field 0x15BE clears when it resets the record. Read at 0x1F60-0x1F70.
0x1f70: step the record's state down from four

takes a record pointer and decrements its byte at 0x1E only when that byte is exactly 4, leaving every other value alone - so it moves one specific state on and is a no-op otherwise. Read at 0x1F70-0x1F82.
0x37d2: blit one fixed graphic to the playfield

calls 0x12078 with two constant arguments: the source 0xBB38A in the image and the destination 0x200004, four bytes into the playfield. No parameters and no state - it draws the same thing to the same place every time. Read at 0x37D2-0x37E8.
0x512: zeroes the word at 0x3E0802, spins until it becomes non-zero, then decrements it and returns. 0x3E0802 is the frame semaphore the interrupt handler sets - the same one CLAUDE.md names in the spin-loop seam - so this is the game's frame wait. Read at 0x512-0x52A.
0x52a: one instruction: writes zero to the frame semaphore at 0x3E0802, without waiting. The bare counterpart of 0x512. Read at 0x52A-0x534.
0x156c: set bits in the second flag word
takes a word on the stack and ORs it into 0x3E0DC8 - a second flag word beside the one at 0x3E0DC6 that 0x1578 and 0x1592 serve. Read at 0x156C-0x1578.
0x1584: clear bits in the second flag word
takes a word on the stack, inverts it, and ANDs it into 0x3E0DC8. Exact counterpart of 0x156C, and the same pairing 0x1578/0x1592 have for 0x3E0DC6. Read at 0x1584-0x1592.
0x618: one instruction: clears the byte at 0x72FFFF. That is the watchdog the board resets by being written to - system.ts names it at 0x72FFFE and treats reads and writes across it as on-map for exactly this reason. Read at 0x618-0x620.
0xfc06: test a word in the protection window

one instruction: tst.w on 0x1400E8, which lies in the window CLAUDE.md records as served by a state machine rather than plain memory - the protection probe's two halves sit at 0x140010 and 0x1400E4. The routine only sets the flags from it; the caller acts on them. Read at 0xFC06-0xFC0E.
0x1578: set bits in the flag word
takes a word on the stack and ORs it into the flag word at 0x3E0DC6. Three instructions. Read at 0x1578-0x1584.
0x1592: clear bits in the flag word
takes a word on the stack, inverts it, and ANDs it into the flag word at 0x3E0DC6 - the exact counterpart of 0x1578. Read at 0x1592-0x15A0.
0x15a0: clear the two high flag bits and set the next

calls 0x1592 with 0x6000 to clear those two bits of the word at 0x3E0DC6, then 0x1578 with 0x1000 to set that one. Renamed 2026-07-31 from 'interrupt mask set', which was wrong: the 68000's interrupt mask lives in the status register, and this touches a word in work RAM. Bits 13 and 14 are alternatives to bit 12 in whatever that word selects. Read at 0x15A0-0x15B4.
0xf2fa: offset from the record table base
three instructions: takes a longword on the stack and returns it minus 0x1F7F0, turning a pointer into a record's own table into an offset from that table's base. Read at 0xF2FA-0xF306.
0x512a: clear the index in every player's object

walks all three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E - with no active check, unlike every other walk here - and for each follows the pointer at field 0x42, stores a word at its start and ORs 0x20 into its byte 2. The word comes from calling 0xF2FA on 0x1F7F0, and 0xF2FA subtracts 0x1F7F0, so the value is exactly zero: the index is being reset rather than set. Field 0x42 therefore points at a per-player object whose first word is an offset into the table at 0x1F7F0. Read at 0x512A-0x5168.
0x482e: gather the stations nobody is playing

walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, and acts on the ones whose field 0 has bit 15 CLEAR - the inverse of every other walk here, so this is about stations that are not in play. For each it copies a byte from the table at 0xFE03 and one from 0xFE07 into a pair at 0x3E1CA6/0x3E1CA7, advancing that destination only for unjoined stations so the result is compacted, then calls 0x48AE. Read at 0x482E-0x4880.
0x4a6a: walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, and for each whose field 0 has bits 14/15 set calls 0xC688 - the routine that writes the palette - passing the table at 0xFE18, the constants 13, 4, 3 and 4, and an index that runs 5, 6, 7, one per station. So each player gets its own palette entries. Read at 0x4A6A-0x4AB8.
0x1c34: run the player flag handler for every active player

walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, and calls 0x5948 - the player flag handler - with each one whose field 0 has bit 15 set. Nothing else. Note the gate is bit 15 alone, where 0x1836 and 0x18FA test bits 14 and 15 together, so this runs for a strictly wider set of players than those do. Read at 0x1C34-0x1C66.
0x149a: does this board cell belong to the player

takes a player struct and a coordinate pair on the stack. Reads the player number from field 0x2, indexes the owner-code table at 0x1000A with it, turns the coordinate into a board cell address through 0x11BD8 (cell address), masks the cell's owner bits with 0xC0, and returns all-ones when they match the player's code and zero when they do not. This is what settles the coordinate pair at fields 0x46/0x47: it is a board cell, and 0x18FA is looking for a starting cell the player already owns. Read at 0x149A-0x14DC.
0x18fa: walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, skipping any whose field 0 lacks bits 14/15. Copies the byte pair at fields 0x48/0x49 into a local, offers it to 0x149A together with the struct, and if that returns non-zero writes the pair into fields 0x46/0x47; otherwise it takes the next pair from the list pointed to by field 0x4A, stepping two bytes at a time, and tries again. 0x46/0x47 is therefore a coordinate pair - the same one 0x1980 writes out scaled by 64 through the pointers at 0x5E and 0x62, whose default 0x19D8 sets to 40. Read at 0x18FA-0x1980.
0x1836: reset the players for a new game

walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E. For each it points field 0x6A at the shot rings (0x3E0F48), clears the ring's first two bytes and marks it 0xFF, and clears byte 0x16 - the value averaged by 0x1A70 - then, if field 0 has bits 14/15 set, clears byte 0x14 (the round), word 0x56 and long 0x28 and calls 0x5948 with the struct. The reset is skipped for the player whose address matches the pointer at 0x3E1C84 when the flag at 0x3E1956 is set, which is how one player is carried over. Read at 0x1836-0x18A6.
0x19d8: reset the player pair to forty

takes a player struct as a stack argument and writes the word 40 through both of its pointers, fields 0x5E and 0x62. It is the default arm of 0x1980, which writes byte 0x46 shifted left six through 0x5E and byte 0x47 the same way through 0x62 when its flag is set. So the two locations hold a paired per-player value that is either derived from 0x46/0x47 or reset to 40; what they mean is still unread. Read at 0x19D8-0x19EE.
0x5e0a: takes a player struct as a stack argument; reads byte 0x2 - the player number, which 0x2248 sets from the loop index - scales it by 128 (asl #6 then doubled), adds it to 0x3E1F1C to pick that player's block, writes 0xFF at the block's first byte, and stores the pointer both at 0x3E209C and in the struct's field 0x66. Read at 0x5E0A-0x5E38.
0x2248: walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, and resets each: clears field 0 (which holds the active bit 15), byte 0x2 and long 0x24; stores the pointers 0x3E080C into 0x5E, 0x3E0814 into 0x62 and 0x3E1888 into 0x7A; calls 0x5E0A with the struct and 0x5B4 with the index; and fills bytes from 0x3E0DCE with 0xFF as it goes. This is where 0x01980's per-player pointers come from. Read at 0x2248-0x22BA.
0x19ee: advance every active player to the next round

walks the three player structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, skipping any whose field 0 lacks bit 15.
